habitat: Semi-arid plains with grass and bare ground, and open grassy plains grazed short, with anthills and low scrub. Also fallow pastures, burnt fields and the edges of saltpans. Usually single or in pairs, with limited winter flocks.
summary: No Newman page. Compared with Plain-backed Pipit it is paler and buffier above, with a warm reddish-buff rump, a less sharply defined pale eyebrow, fainter breast markings, and buffy belly and flanks. The juvenile has mottles. Wikipedia says the lower mandible has a pinkish base. SABAP1 says the base of the lower mandible is yellow. That conflict is left unresolved. No length is given. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

bill.shape: The lower-mandible base is pinkish in Wikipedia and yellow in SABAP1, so no bill colour is stored.

head.pattern: Pale eyebrow, less sharply defined than in Plain-backed Pipit.

upperparts.pattern: Paler and buffier above than Plain-backed Pipit. Rump warm reddish buff.

underparts.pattern: Faint breast markings. Belly and flanks buffy. Ventral streaking is further reduced than in Plain-backed Pipit.

upperparts.pattern: Wikipedia says the juvenile has mottles and does not describe the colours.

calls.description: The sources used do not describe the call. The only openly licensed grade B recording has a filename that includes a grebe, so it was not used. Grade C call from open veld near Polokwane, Limpopo. The filename is XC444076-01BuffyPipit_Polokwane_20181117.MP3.

research.note: No Newman page. SABAP1 describes breeding races and winter flocks and does not use the word resident, so status and months are unset. The bill-base colour conflicts between Wikipedia and SABAP1. Wikipedia’s length sentence is blank. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Plain-backed Pipit is darker above, with a sharper white eyebrow, a longer hind claw and a yellowish bill base.
